log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
Lead: 34% BRING: dragapult, 26% BRING: gholdengo, 25% BRING: aegislash
Pick 2: 54% BRING: gholdengo, 22% BRING: aegislash, 10% BRING: corviknight
Pick 3: 38% BRING: aegislash, 25% BRING: corviknight, 23% BRING: kingambit

Opponent is 5 Steel-types plus Dragapult, so Fire plus Ground coverage is the deciding factor. Incineroar handles Corviknight and Kingambit that wall Garchomp, a bad matchup to avoid alone. Dragonite adds Ice Punch and ExtremeSpeed for Dragapult speed control.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Reviewing Pokémon battle rules and formatting requirements for the single best turn action.Parsing team composition and move sets to identify legal bring options for turn one.Evaluating type coverage and speed tiers to finalize the three-Pokémon bring and lead order.Adjusting the lead choice due to Fake Out immunity against Ghost types and selecting Dragonite for priority and coverage.

decisions.thought: 29% SWITCH: aegislash, 20% MOVE: thunderbolt, 18% SWITCH: gholdengo

Incineroar is a bad matchup into Dragapult since Fake Out is immune and Flare Blitz is resisted. Preserving Incineroar for the Steel-heavy backline matters. Parting Shot pivots out while weakening Dragapult.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing Pokemon type matchups and move legality to determine valid first-turn actions.Evaluating type interactions and ability interactions to rule out ineffective moves.Comparing Parting Shot pivot versus hard switch while accounting for Clear Body and type immunities.

decisions.thought: Dragonite's Flying type is a bad matchup to switch into Aegislash Steel STAB, while Garchomp takes it neutrally. Garchomp also threatens a super effective STAB Earthquake and preserves Dragonite's Multiscale and Extremespeed for Dragapult.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Summarizing the Pokémon battle constraints and decision format for a single-turn action selection.Evaluating legal single-turn actions against opponent state and format constraints.Comparing switch options using type matchup, speed, and ability interactions.Evaluating defensive type matchup and preserving Multiscale for the faster Dragapult threat.

decisions.thought: 31% SWITCH: dragapult, 25% SWITCH: gholdengo, 22% MOVE: kingsshield
Garchomp is faster than Aegislash but King's Shield has priority and would block a super-effective Earthquake. At -1 Aegislash can't knockout Garchomp, so setting up punishes the shield.

decisions.thought: 33% MOVE: dragondarts, 21% SWITCH: gholdengo, 19% MOVE: shadowball

Dragapult is likely faster than Garchomp and threatens a knockout with a super-effective Dragon move. Losing our +2 sweeper would be costly. Mega evolving behind Protect scouts safely while keeping boosts.

decisions.thought: 67% MOVE: dragondarts, 19% SWITCH: aegislash, 14% SWITCH: gholdengo
At +2 Attack, Dragon Claw should knockout frail Dragapult. Even if Dragapult is faster, full HP Mega Garchomp survives one Dragon Darts.

decisions.thought: 57% SWITCH: aegislash, 43% SWITCH: gholdengo
34% MOVE: sacredsword, 31% SWITCH: gholdengo, 17% MOVE: shadowball
We move first and +2 STAB super-effective Earthquake should knock out Shield-form Aegislash. Even priority Shadow Sneak from Shield form cannot KO our 57 HP.

decisions.thought: 47% MOVE: sacredsword, 36% SWITCH: gholdengo, 13% MOVE: kingsshield

We outspeed Aegislash but its sash is broken and it is at 1% HP, so it likely goes for priority Shadow Sneak to knock out our 12 HP Garchomp. Protect blocks that knockout and keeps our +2 Attack for next turn.

decisions.thought: 50% SWITCH: gholdengo, 35% MOVE: sacredsword, 12% MOVE: kingsshield

Garchomp at 12 HP moves first with Earthquake but likely gets knocked out by Aegislash priority Shadow Sneak. This is a bad matchup to stay in, so switch to a Ghost resist to preserve Garchomp and KO next turn.

decisions.thought: 55% MOVE: nastyplot, 19% MOVE: steelbeam, 17% MOVE: shadowball
Flare Blitz is super effective and likely knocks out Gholdengo. Fake Out is immune and status moves are blocked by Good as Gold, so staying in to attack is best.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating Incineroar's Parting Shot against Gholdengo's Good as Gold ability and choosing the optimal move.Assessing Gholdengo's likely STAB and Focus Blast damage versus Incineroar's Fire/Dark resistances.

decisions.thought: 100% SWITCH: aegislash
64% MOVE: sacredsword, 31% MOVE: kingsshield, 3% MOVE: swordsdance
Aegislash is at 1% as opponent's last Pokemon, so a super-effective Flare Blitz is a likely knockout to end the game. Speed is uncertain but even a trade still wins with Dragonite in back.
